facts.statement: Mapusaurus fossils were found in a bonebed containing seven to nine individuals excavated between 1997 and 2001 in Argentina.
facts.quote: It is known from a bonebed of between seven and nine specimens, excavated from the strata of the Huincul Formation between 1997 and 2001 as part of the Argentinian-Canadian Dinosaur Project.

facts.statement: The first Mapusaurus fossils were discovered in 1997 at Cañadón del Gato, located 20 km south of Plaza Huincul in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The first fossils of this taxon were discovered in 1997 by members of the Argentinian-Canadian Dinosaur Project in an exposure of the Huincul Formation at Cañadón del Gato, a site 20 km south of Plaza Huincul in Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus resembled Giganotosaurus but possessed a deeper skull, a rougher maxilla, a textured lacrimal bone, and differently proportioned neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus generally resembled Giganotosaurus, though had a deeper skull, a more rugose maxilla, a rougher surface to its lacrimal bone, differently proportioned neck vertebrae, and various other minor differences.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus had very small arms proportional to those of tyrannosaurids and abelisaurids.
facts.quote: The arms of Mapusaurus were very small, similar in terms of proportional size to those of tyrannosaurids and abelisaurids.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus coexisted with giant titanosaurs like Argentinosaurus and Choconsaurus, along with rebbachisaurids, unenlagiids, and ceratosaurs.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus itself coexisted with the giant titanosaurs Argentinosaurus and Choconsaurus, as well as a menagerie of rebbachisaurids, unenlagiids, and ceratosaurs.

facts.statement: The largest known Mapusaurus specimen, identified by a left femur, was originally estimated to reach 10.2 meters in length and weigh 3 tons.
facts.quote: Based on the biggest specimen known from the bonebed, represented by a left femur, it was originally estimated to have reached a maximum body length of 10.2 m and a mass of 3 t.

facts.statement: Later studies revised the maximum size estimates for Mapusaurus to between 10.2 and 12.6 meters in length and 6 to 8 tons in mass.
facts.quote: Subsequent works have given maximum size estimates of 10.2 - 12.6 m and 6 - 8 t, respectively.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Mapusaurus roseae is an isolated right nasal bone cataloged as MCF-PVPH-108.1.
facts.quote: Coria and Currie designated an isolated right nasal (MCF-PVPH-108.1, Museo Carmen Funes, Paleontología de Vertebrados) as the holotype (name-bearing) specimen of M. roseae.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus fossils include parts of the skull, teeth, vertebrae, pelvis, ribs, hindlimbs, foot bones, and fragments of the forelimb.
facts.quote: In total, Mapusaurus is known from parts of the skull and mandible, teeth, some cervical (neck), dorsal (back) and caudal vertebrae, much of the sacrum and pelvis, some ribs, parts of the scapulocoracoid, much of the hindlimbs, many pedal phalanges, and fragments of the forelimb and manus.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Taurovenator is a synonym of Mapusaurus because they found no unique distinguishing traits in the Taurovenator holotype.
facts.quote: Coria and colleagues (2019) suggested that Taurovenator is a synonym of Mapusaurus, as they found no autapomorphies (distinguishing traits) unique to MPCA-Pv 803.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Taurovenator and Mapusaurus are distinct genera, as they are found in different stratigraphic units of the Huincul Formation.
facts.quote: However, Taurovenator is actually from the lower unit of the Huincul Formation, while Mapusaurus is from the upper unit of the formation, suggesting they could be distinct genera.

facts.statement: Coria and Currie estimated that Mapusaurus specimens in the bonebed ranged from 5.5 to 10.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: In their paper describing Mapusaurus, Coria and Currie estimated that the specimens found in the bonebed measured between 5.5–10.2 m in length.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus had a skull that was deeper and narrower than that of Giganotosaurus.
facts.quote: The skull of Mapusaurus was deeper and narrower than that of Giganotosaurus, due to the comparative shortness of the maxillae and slenderness of the nasal bones.

facts.statement: Each maxilla of Mapusaurus contained 12 tooth sockets, fewer than the 14 found in Carcharodontosaurus.
facts.quote: There were 12 alveoli (tooth sockets) in each maxilla, as opposed to 14 in Carcharodontosaurus.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Mapusaurus appears to have held fifteen teeth.
facts.quote: Each dentary appears to have had fifteen teeth.

facts.statement: The second neck vertebra of Mapusaurus had a neural spine that was longer and more slender than those of the species itself, likely a comparison error in the source text implying it was longer and more gracile than in other related forms.
facts.quote: The neural spine (the tall projections at the top of each vertebra) of the axis, the second cervical (neck) vertebra, appears to have been longer and more gracile than those of Mapusaurus.

facts.statement: The rear back vertebrae of Mapusaurus were amphicoelus, having flat surfaces on both the front and back.
facts.quote: The more posterior dorsal vertebrae were amphicoelus, meaning that both anterior and posterior surfaces were flat.

facts.statement: Rib anatomy suggests that the chest of Mapusaurus was deeper than it was wide.
facts.quote: The anatomy of the preserved ribs, which resemble those of many other large theropods, suggests that the chest of Mapusaurus would have been deeper than it was wide.

facts.statement: In Mapusaurus, the shoulder blade and coracoid remained as separate bones rather than fusing together.
facts.quote: The scapula and coracoid were distinct bones, and did not co-ossify into a scapulocoracoid.

facts.statement: The upper arm bone of Mapusaurus was about one-quarter the length of the thigh bone, indicating relatively short arms.
facts.quote: The humerus was around a quarter of the length of the femur, and its arms were thus relatively short.

facts.statement: The radius, one of the forearm bones, was relatively massive in Mapusaurus.
facts.quote: The radius (one of the two forearm bones) was relatively massive.

facts.statement: The second and third hand bones of Mapusaurus appear to have been partly fused, but the first hand bone did not fuse with them.
facts.quote: The second and third metacarpals (hand bones) appear to have been partly fused, though there is no indication that the first metacarpal had fused with the others.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus had a prominent fourth trochanter on the thigh bone, unlike most other carnosaurs.
facts.quote: Unlike most other carnosaurs, the fourth trochanter, one of the structures to which the caudofemoralis muscles would have attached, was prominent.

facts.statement: The fibula of Mapusaurus was slightly more slender than that of the holotype of Giganotosaurus.
facts.quote: The fibula, the other lower leg bone, was slightly more gracile than in the holotype of Giganotosaurus.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows eight foot bones in Mapusaurus, but no claw bones from the foot have been preserved.
facts.quote: Eight pedal (foot) phalanges are represented, though no pedal unguals are preserved.

facts.statement: Researchers speculated that the bonebed might represent a predator trap or a coincidental accumulation of carcasses, though this remains a hypothesis.
facts.quote: Coria and Currie (2006) speculated that this may represent a long-term, possibly coincidental, accumulation of carcasses (some sort of predator trap) and may provide clues about Mapusaurus behavior.

facts.statement: The bonebed may provide the first substantive evidence of gregarious behavior in large theropods, though it is unknown if they hunted in organized packs or as a mob.
facts.quote: If so, this would be the first substantive evidence of gregarious behavior by large theropods, although whether theropods of that size hunted in organized packs or simply attacked in a mob is unknown.

facts.statement: A cervical vertebra in the fossil assemblage suffered from an infection possibly similar to tuberculosis.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebra suffered form an infection of some kind, possibly similar to tuberculosis.

facts.statement: Two ribs were fractured and rehealed, likely belonging to an older individual.
facts.quote: The two ribs were fractured and rehealed, likely coming from an older individual.

facts.statement: Healed fractures indicate that Mapusaurus lived a hazardous and active lifestyle similar to many theropods.
facts.quote: This indicates that Mapusaurus, like many theropods, lived a hazardous, active lifestyle.

facts.statement: Only 2.8% of Mapusaurus fossils bore pathologies, representing just 11.1% of the total individuals.
facts.quote: Only 2.8% of the Mapusaurus fossils bore pathologies and came from at least one individual and just 11.1% of the total individuals.

facts.statement: Analysis suggests that none of the observed diseases caused the death of the individuals in the bonebed.
facts.quote: Based on the taphonomic setting of the bonebed, none of these diseases were the causes of death for those individuals.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus is classified as a genus in the family Carcharodontosauridae, subfamily Carcharodontosaurinae, and tribe Giganotosaurini.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus is a genus in the family Carcharodontosauridae, subfamily Carcharodontosaurinae, and tribe Giganotosaurini.

facts.statement: The tribe Giganotosaurini is endemic to the Late Cretaceous of Argentina and includes some of the largest known theropods.
facts.quote: Giganotosaurini is a tribe of giant carcharodontosaurines endemic to the Late Cretaceous of Argentina, with some members like Giganotosaurus possibly being the largest theropods known, reaching sizes as large as 13.2 m in length and 4.2 to 13.8 MT in mass.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in Argentina.
facts.quote: Giganotosaurini is a tribe of giant carcharodontosaurines endemic to the Late Cretaceous of Argentina

facts.statement: The subfamily Carcharodontosaurinae was likely restricted to the southern continent of Gondwana, where they were probably the apex predators.
facts.quote: The subfamily Carcharodontosaurinae, in which Carcharodontosaurus belongs, appears to have been restricted to the southern continent of Gondwana (formed by South America and Africa), where they were probably the apex predators.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus was discovered in the Argentine Province of Neuquén.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus was discovered in the Argentine Province of Neuquén.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus fossils were found in the Lower Cretaceous Huincul Formation, which consists of fine-to-medium grain sandstones.
facts.quote: The Huincul Formation is composed of yellowish and greenish sandstones of fine-to-medium grain, some of which are tuffaceous. These deposits were laid down during the Lower Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The genus Mapusaurus was named by Coria and Currie in 2006.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Coria y Currie, 2006

facts.statement: Based on the largest specimen found, Mapusaurus is estimated to have been 12.2 to 12.6 meters long and weighed up to 6.8 tonnes.
facts.quote: Basándose en las proporciones del espécimen más grande encontrado, se ha estimado que Mapusaurus roseae medía de 12,2 a 12,6 m de longitud y que pesaba hasta 6,8 toneladas.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus was a large theropod similar in size to Giganotosaurus, with known individuals reaching approximately 10.2 meters in length and weighing about three tonnes.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus era un gran terópodo y era más o menos similar en tamaño a su pariente cercano Giganotosaurus, con los individuos más grandes conocidos de aproximadamente 10,2 m de longitud o más y un peso de aproximadamente tres toneladas.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus remains were excavated between 1997 and 2001 by the Argentine-Canadian Proyecto Dinosaurio expedition.
facts.quote: Los restos de Mapusaurus fueron exhumados entre 1997 y 2001 por la expedición argentino-canadiense Proyecto Dinosaurio

facts.statement: The excavation was led by Argentine paleontologist Rodolfo Coria and his Canadian colleague Philip Currie.
facts.quote: Los responsables de la extracción fueron el profesor paleontólogo argentino Rodolfo Coria y su colega canadiense Philip Currie

facts.statement: The species was named in honor of the Mapuche people inhabiting the region and was publicly announced in 2006.
facts.quote: quienes lo bautizaron en honor a la etnia mapuche que habita la región e hicieron público el descubrimiento en 2006

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that the fossil site may represent a long-term accumulation of remains, possibly due to a natural trap, offering clues about Mapusaurus behavior.
facts.quote: Coria y Currie han especulado que el nicho del hallazgo puede representar una acumulación de restos de largo plazo (posiblemente debido a una cierta clase de trampa natural), y podría proporcionar pistas sobre el comportamiento de Mapusaurus.

facts.statement: It remains debated whether Mapusaurus hunted in organized groups or simply attacked in bands, as the specific hunting mechanism is unknown.
facts.quote: aunque el mecanismo concreto de caza permanece desconocido, ya que no queda claro si lo hacían en grupos organizados o si simplemente atacaban en banda.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus is diagnosed as a carcharodontosaurid theropod with a skull differing from Giganotosaurus by having thick, rugose nasal bones, narrower anterior portions, a greater extension of the antorbital fossa, and smaller maxillary fenestrae.
facts.quote: Coria y Currie en 2006 diagnostican Mapusaurus como un terópodo carcarodontosáurido cuyo cráneo difiere de Giganotosaurus en que tiene huesos nasales gruesos y rugosos, más angostos en la porción anterior a la unión nasal/maxilar/lagrimal, posee una mayor extensión de la fosa anteorbital hacia el maxilar y menores fenestras maxilares

facts.statement: Mapusaurus is unique in having the upper squamosal-yugal process of the yugal bone divided into two small anterior parts and a milohioide foramen at the contact between the dentary and splenial.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus roseae es único en que el proceso de la parte superior cuadrado-yugal del yugal se divide en dos pequeños anteriores, un foramen milohioideo sobre el contacto del dentario con el esplenial.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus features fused second and third metacarpals and a humerus with a wide distal end and little separation between the condyles.
facts.quote: El segundo y tercer metacarpianos fusionados, húmero con el extremo distal amplio y con poca separación en medio de los cóndilos.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus differs from Giganotosaurus by having conical epiphyses that are slightly curved in the cervicals and taper toward the distal end.
facts.quote: También se diferencia de Giganotosaurus en tener las epipófisis cónicas, levemente curvadas en las cervicales que se afilan hacia el extremo distal.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus vertebrae have a notable sharp dorsal margin on the dorsal spines, which are tall and wider.
facts.quote: Un notable margen dorsal agudo de las espinas dorsales de las vértebras, que son altas, más anchas.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus has a curved ischial shaft and a thinner fibula.
facts.quote: EL eje isquiático es curvado y un peroné más delgado

facts.statement: Mapusaurus fossils were excavated between 1997 and 2001 by the Argentine-Canadian Dinosaur Project from the Huincul Formation at Cañadón El Gato.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus fue excavado entre 1997 y 2001, por el Proyecto dinosaurio Argentino-Canadiense, de un afloramiento de la Formación Huincul en el Subgrupo Río Limay en Cañadón El Gato.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus was described and named by paleontologists Rodolfo Coria and Philip Currie in 2006.
facts.quote: Fue descrito y nombrado por los paleontólogos Rodolfo Coria y Philip Currie en 2006.

facts.statement: The name Mapusaurus is derived from the Mapudungun word mapu, meaning 'of the earth', and the Greek word saurus, meaning 'lizard'.
facts.quote: El nombre Mapusaurus deriva del mapudungun mapu, que significa "de la tierra", y del griego saurus, "lagarto".

facts.statement: The species Mapusaurus roseae was named after the pink rocks where fossils were found and after Rose Letwin, who sponsored the expeditions.
facts.quote: La especie hallada, Mapusaurus roseae, fue bautizada así por lleva el nombre de las rocas de color rosa, en las que se encontraron los fósiles y de Rose Letwin, que patrocinó las expediciones que recuperaron estos fósiles.

facts.statement: Removing the petrified sediments covering approximately 300 bones took five months of work.
facts.quote: La obra de remoción de los sedimentos petrificados que cubrían los aproximadamente 300 huesos demandó cinco meses de trabajo.

facts.statement: The holotype for Mapusaurus roseae is an isolated right nasal bone, MCF-PVPH-108.1, housed at the Carmen Funes Museum in Huincul, Neuquén.
facts.quote: El holotipo designado para el género y especie, Mapusaurus roseae, es un hueso nasal derecho aislado, MCF-PVPH-108.1, alojado en el Museo Carmen Funes, Paleontología de Vertebrados, Huincul, Neuquén.

facts.statement: Twelve paratypes have been named based on various disconnected bone elements.
facts.quote: Doce paratipos han sido nombrados basados en diferentes elementos óseos inconexos.

facts.statement: Taken together, all these fragments make up most of the animal's complete skeleton.
facts.quote: Tomados juntos, todos estos fragmentos componen la mayor parte del esqueleto completo del animal.

facts.statement: The discovery site at Cañadón del Gato is interpreted as a freshwater deposit accumulated by an ephemeral or seasonal stream in an arid or semi-arid region.
facts.quote: El lugar del hallazgo en el Cañadón del Gato se interpreta como un depósito de agua dulce, "acumulado por una corriente efímera o estacional en una región con clima árido o semiárido".

facts.statement: Wider press coverage of the discovery was given on April 17, 2006.
facts.quote: El 17 de abril de 2006, se dio una publicidad de prensa más amplia al hallazgo.

facts.statement: It was falsely claimed that Mapusaurus was the largest known carnivorous dinosaur, and earlier speculations about pack hunting were repeated, though taphonomic analysis showed the skeletons were not buried at once.
facts.quote: El tamaño de Mapusaurus fue exagerado, se hizo la falsa afirmación de que era el dinosaurio carnívoro más grande conocido, y se repitieron las especulaciones previas sobre la caza en grupos, aunque el análisis tafonómico de los hallazgos demostró claramente que los diversos esqueletos no fueron enterrados de una sola vez.

facts.statement: Cladistic studies by Coria and Currie show that Mapusaurus belongs to the Carcharodontosauridae, with femur structure suggesting a closer relationship to Giganotosaurus than to Carcharodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Estudios cladísticos realizados por Coria y Currie demuestran definitivamente que Mapusaurus está dentro del grupo de los Carcharodontosauridae, observándose que la estructura del fémur sugiere una relación más cercana con Giganotosaurus de lo que cualquiera de los dos taxones comparte con Carcharodontosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers proposed the monophyletic subfamily Giganotosaurinae, defined as all carcharodontosaurids more closely related to Giganotosaurus and Mapusaurus than to Carcharodontosaurus.
facts.quote: Los investigadores proponen una nueva taxonomía monofilética basada en esta relación: la subfamilia Giganotosaurinae, definida como todos los carcarodontosáuridos más cercanos a Giganotosaurus y Mapusaurus que a Carcharodontosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2013, a review by Novas et al. reorganized several Carcharodontosauridae genera, changing the subfamily from Giganotosaurinae to Carcharodontosaurinae.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, en 2013 una revisión hecha por Novas et al., reordenó a varios de los géneros conocidos de la familia Carcharodontosauridae, en esta revisión se cambió a la subfamilia Giganotosaurinae por la Carcharodontosaurinae.

facts.statement: This new subfamily includes only carcharodontosaurids that inhabited South America and Africa and lived between the Aptian and Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Esta nueva subfamilia, solo están incluidos los carcarodontosáuridos que habitaron en Suramérica y África y que vivieron entre el Aptiano y el Cenomaniano.

facts.statement: The three last mentioned genera, which correspond only to Patagonian taxa, were reassigned to a new tribe called Giganotosaurini.
facts.quote: Y los tres últimos mencionados, los cuales corresponden solo a taxones patagónicos, fueron reasignados en una nueva tribu llamada Giganotosaurini.

facts.statement: These three genera share features such as a postorbital process of the jugal with a wide anteroposterior base, no pleurocoels in caudal vertebrae, and femur characteristics like a reduced fourth trochanter or a poorly defined cross-crest in the distal zone.
facts.quote: Estos tres géneros comparten entre sí varias características, como un proceso postorbital del yugal con una base amplia en sentido anteroposterior (desde el frente hasta la parte de atrás), no tienen pleurocelos en las vértebras caudales, y varias características del fémur como un cuarto trocánter reducido o una cresta cruzada mal definida en la zona distal también los asemejan.

facts.statement: The Huincul Formation is believed to represent an arid environment with ephemeral or seasonal streams, dated to 97 to 93.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Como se mencionó anteriormente, se cree que la Formación Huincul representa un ambiente árido con corrientes efímeras o estacionales. La edad de esta formación se estima en 97 a 93,5 millones de años.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus shared its environment with the sauropods Argentinosaurus, one of the largest if not the largest sauropods, and Cathartesaura.
facts.quote: Mapusaurus compartió su entorno con los saurópodos Argentinosaurus, uno de los saurópodos más grandes, si no el más grande y Cathartesaura.

facts.statement: The abelisauroid theropods Skorpiovenator and Ilokelesia also lived in the region.
facts.quote: Los terópodos abelisauroides Skorpiovenator e Ilokelesia también vivían en la región.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus fossils were found in a bone bed containing at least seven individuals of various growth stages.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles de Mapusaurus fueron descubiertos en un lecho óseo que contenía al menos siete individuos de diversas etapas de crecimiento.

facts.statement: Coria and Currie speculated that this could represent a long-term accumulation of carcasses, possibly by chance, some type of predator trap, and may provide clues about Mapusaurus behavior.
facts.quote: Coria y Currie especularon que esto podría representar una acumulación de cadáveres a largo plazo, posiblemente por coincidencia, algún tipo de trampa de depredador y puede proporcionar pistas sobre el comportamiento de Mapusaurus.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Rodolfo Coria suggested in a press conference that this bone congregation might indicate Mapusaurus hunted in groups and worked together to take down large prey like the massive sauropod Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo Rodolfo Coria, del Museo Carmen Funes, contrario a su artículo publicado, repitió en una conferencia de prensa sugerencias anteriores de que esta congregación de huesos fósiles podría indicar que Mapusaurus cazaba en grupos y trabajaba en conjunto para derribar presas grandes, como el inmenso saurópodo Argentinosaurus.

facts.statement: If true, this would be the first substantial evidence of gregarious behavior in large theropods other than Tyrannosaurus, though it is unknown if they hunted in organized packs like wolves or simply attacked in a horde.
facts.quote: Si es así, esta sería la primera evidencia sustancial de comportamiento gregario por parte de grandes terópodos que no sean Tyrannosaurus, aunque se desconoce si podrían haber cazado en manadas organizadas, como lo hacen los lobos, o simplemente haber atacado en una horda.

facts.statement: A 2014 ontogenetic study by Canale et al. found that Mapusaurus showed heterochrony, an evolutionary condition where animals retain an ancestral trait during a life stage but lose it as they develop.
facts.quote: Un estudio ontogenético de Canale et al en 2014 encontró que Mapusaurus mostró heterocronía, una condición evolutiva en la cual los animales pueden retener una característica ancestral durante una etapa de su vida, pero la pierden a medida que se desarrollan.

facts.statement: In Mapusaurus, maxillary fenestrae are present in younger individuals but gradually disappear as they mature.
facts.quote: En Mapusaurus, las fenestras maxilares están presentes en individuos más jóvenes, pero desaparecen gradualmente a medida que maduran.

facts.statement: Mapusaurus lived during the Albian stage, from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Mapusaurus is Carcharodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Carcharodontosauridae

facts.statement: Mapusaurus belongs to the family Carcharodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Carcharodontosauridae

facts.statement: Mapusaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
